タイトル: Faster Payments Needed to Support Local Tour Operators in Madagascar
投稿者: RAONIZANANY マダガスカルのTravel Agent レジャー、旅行、観光, 2～10人規模の会社 使用期間： 2年以上 共有 "Faster Payments Needed to Support Local Tour Operators in Madagascar"
良い点: What I liked most about Bókun was its all-in-one booking management system. It makes it easier to manage tour availability, reservations, payments, and customer information in one place. I also appreciated its integration with online booking platforms, which helps reach more customers and streamline daily tour operations.
改善点: The biggest disadvantage of Bókun for us is the delay in receiving payments. Since our tours operate in Madagascar, we often have to wait up to one month to receive our funds in our local bank account. This creates cash-flow difficulties and affects our ability to organize and operate tours smoothly. I strongly recommend that Bókun introduce faster and more flexible payment methods, allowing tour operators in Madagascar to receive their payments within 4 business days. Faster payouts would greatly improve cash flow, help us pay local suppliers on time, and ensure better service for our clients.

改善点: Maintenance during business hours without any notification toward operators, resellers, and administrators. Synchronisation issues between Bókun and operators on what is available and what is not (group size/vehicle capacity etc.) resulting in extremely iffy situations with clients as well as between operators and resellers. Less enthusiastic customer support, available only during banking hours, definitely not on weekends. No updates on changes regarding bookings in the system - unless one does everything in triples: updating Bókun, notifying the operator, wait for confirmatiom from operator, notify client. Key-word search is quite cumbersome. Software getting less and less user-friendly with every update. Inability to edit certain aspects of bookings and the invoice, so one has to cancel everything, and re-book, while keeping their fingers crossed that the re-booking will work and no one will take the seats while Bókun is thinking its life through.
